sources.name: OGC Abstract Specification Topic 20: Observations, measurements and samples 3.0
sources.role: observation result, procedure, observed property, feature of interest and sampling contract
verified_facts: An observation describes an estimate of an observed property of a feature of interest, produced by applying a procedure.
Observation time, procedure, observed property, feature of interest and result are distinct parts of the observation description.
The model records how an observation or measurement value came to be; sampling features may act as proxies for other features.
semantic_limits: A numeric result without its procedure, observed property, feature of interest and time bindings is not parcel-elevation evidence.
A result observed on a sample or sampling feature must not be silently transferred to an HMLR parcel.
OMS model conformance describes observation semantics; it does not independently certify calibration, source authority or accuracy.

sources.name: OGC SensorML Encoding Standard 3.0
sources.role: physical/non-physical process, input, output, parameter, configuration and connection contract
verified_facts: SensorML models physical and non-physical processes through AbstractProcess-derived classes.
A process can declare inputs, outputs and parameters; methodology and parameter settings transform inputs into outputs.
SensorML 3.0 defines JSON models and encodings and uses SWE Common data components for process inputs, outputs and parameters.
semantic_limits: A SensorML process description or connected processing chain is not proof that the instrument was calibrated for the candidate measurement.
A Quantity output remains fail-closed until its source observation, unit, reference frame, procedure version and provenance are bound.
Process configuration or successful execution must not create a business row without independent measurement evidence.

sources.name: OGC TimeseriesML 1.3 — XML Encoding of the Timeseries Profile of Observations and Measurements
sources.role: time-value pair, domain-range, chronological order, point metadata and null-value contract
verified_facts: TimeseriesML supports time-value-pair and domain-range encodings for observation results.
Timeseries points are required to be ordered in increasing time in the relevant conformance classes.
A null point is explicitly marked as nil and is accompanied by a reason; measurement-series values use measure or quantity content models.
semantic_limits: A schema-valid timeseries does not prove that its values are authoritative parcel-height observations.
A null, missing or unknown point must never be converted to zero or carried forward as a measured height.
Default point metadata, temporal ordering and XML conformance do not replace source version, vertical datum, geometry and procedure validation.

sources.name: OGC SWE Common Data Model Encoding Standard 3.0
sources.role: quantity, unit, scale, reference frame, nil value, quality and data encoding contract
verified_facts: A continuous numerical representation consists of a decimal value together with its scale or unit of measure.
A Quantity declares a mandatory unit; if a UCUM code and external unit reference are both supplied, they identify the same unit.
NilValues reserve values for unavailable measurements and bind each reserved value to a reason; data descriptions may be paired with JSON, text or binary encodings.
semantic_limits: Binary, text or JSON encoding conformance does not validate measurement semantics, authority or completeness.
A nil value is not a numeric measurement and must be excluded from minimum, maximum and height-difference calculations.
A metre unit alone does not identify EPSG:5701, ODN semantics, exact parcel geometry or source accuracy.
